messages: nina: Quick heads-up — ran a fresh smoke for the new quant4x reranker on the 'short-queries-lite' cohort and saw MRR drop concentrated in queries <6 tokens; NDCG@10 ~unchanged. Anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking: jorge: numbers? nina: fp16 -> MRR 0.438 NDCG@10 0.741; quant4x -> MRR 0.397 NDCG@10 0.739. top1 share down ~6 points. pat: that smells like tokenization/normalization mismatch or tie-breaking compression. Did the candidate normalizer change? jorge: we merged normalizer v3 last week to preserve inline code tags and newlines for structured answers. Could affect first-token splits. nina: sample diff: candidate text older: "answer: 42" new: "answer:\n42" — changes initial tokens for many short candidates. pat: tokenizer bump too? tokenizers 0.13.0 rolled in on 3056700000 build. Token splits for "<" and code tags changed. iris: can you run fp16 on the new candidates to isolate whether normalization alone causes delta? nina: starting fp16 + candidates_v3 run now (mini cohort 5k). command: `python -m eval.run --cohort short-queries-lite --model fp16 --candidates candidates_v3.json --metrics mrr,ndcg` eval-bot: queued run -> https://ci.redwood/evals/3056789012/short-queries-lite (artifacts + per-query CSV). (12m) neval: interim: fp16+candidates_v3 MRR 0.437 (same as baseline fp16@v2), quant4x+candidates_v3 MRR 0.398. so candidates_v3 alone not the full cause. jorge: interesting. try pretokenized inputs (force ids) with quant4x on v3. If pretokenized matches fp16, it's runtime tokenization mismatch; if not, quant numerics. pat: also capture token counts and prefix tokens for first 20 candidates so we can compare distributions. nina: kicked pretokenized run: `--pretokenize --tokenizer_sha=spm-1.4.2` eval-bot: queued pretokenized job 3056789045 -> expected finish ~8m. (8m) pretest: quant4x + pretokenized -> MRR 0.436 (matches fp16). iris: bingo. That points to tokenizer/runtime mismatch. Likely the deployed quant runtime uses a different tokenizer binary/version or applies extra normalization. jorge: we should surface tokenizer SHA in the model manifest and fail evaluation if mismatch. Also add a small CI check that compares tokenized ids between fp16 and quant Docker images for a canonical set. pat: short-term mitigation: for onboarding lanes force pretokenize until we pin tokenizer versions. Also revert normalizer v3 for short-query cohorts if pretokenize not feasible. nina: agreed. I'll open a rollback PR for normalizer v3 for onboarding and add a ticket for tokenizer-sha enforcement. mike: small suggestion — add a quick smoke: pick 500 canonical short queries and assert top1 parity within 1% between fp16 and quant when pretokenized flag off. Fail if mismatch > threshold. jorge: +1. Also log tie-rate (pairs within 0.001) and tokenization-diff-rate per run. If tie-rate spikes with quant, that's a separate signal. pat: prod note: deploys sometimes yank a newer tokenizer in the infra image; infra should not silently change tokenizer binary in production lanes. @infra-team please make tokenizer an explicit image dependency. iris: filing tasks: - (nina) rollback normalizer v3 for onboarding short-query cohort PR - (jorge) add tokenizer_sha validation to eval harness + manifest - (pat) add pretokenize smoke test & tie-rate check in rankbench - (mike) CI canonical short-query parity test - (infra) pin tokenizer in model-serving images nina: marking quant4x promotion blocked until we land the short-term mitigations. Will update ticket when rollback merges. :white_check_mark:
